corpusSummary: A diverse 2026 corpus of social-science papers on large language models spans health, education, policy, climate, and everyday human–AI interactions. Across these records, researchers emphasize ethics, equity, and governance; pedagogy, trust, literacy, and safe deployment in learning; human–AI embodiment and social dynamics; and methodological innovation, using LLMs for coding, data analysis, simulations, and policy study. Calls for validation, transparency, and responsible, accessible AI remain prominent.

themes.name: Ethics, equity, and governance of generative AI in society
themes.description: A synthesis of governance, ethics, and equity concerns across health, education, and AI deployments, emphasizing equity-first governance, cultural adequacy, bias mitigation, and transparent, standardized oversight.

themes.name: AI in education and learning: trust, literacy, and pedagogy
themes.description: Examines AI-enabled tutoring, counseling, assessment, and classroom integration, highlighting trust, AI literacy, dependency risks, and design frameworks to support effective, ethical learning.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, embodiment, and social dynamics
themes.description: Explores how users perceive AI as social actors through embodiment, humanness-empathy tensions, trust, adoption, and the emergence of social dynamics in simulations and everyday interactions.

themes.name: AI methods, tools, and methodological rigor in social science
themes.description: Charts how LLMs and AI tools reshape coding, data analysis, simulations, and policy research, stressing validation, transparency, ethics, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

emergingKeywords: trust and embodiment in human–AI interaction
